intro.about: LeanFM checks requirements before code exists. A project's specification is a list of named requirements: protocols (interactions between roles, drawn as diagrams), CTL formulas over them, and deployments. Every requirement reduces to CTL and stands proved (by the model checker), tested (a run of an implementation meets it), sorry (nothing shows it yet) or failing. Runs, logs and charts of a running project are judged against the same requirements.

intro.rule: Features need strong implication, (leadsTo a b) or (stronglyImplies a b): the trigger a must be able to happen. Security guarantees need weak implication, (weaklyImplies a b): a trigger that never happens is fine. The difference is (possibly a), which CTL can say and LTL cannot.
